newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania plans privatisation of Tarom airline.
newsitem.headline: Romania plans privatisation of Tarom airline.

text.p: Romania has launched a plan to privatise the state airline Tarom, with a 49 percent stake to be sold to a foreign investor and the rest through the stock exchange, a government official said on Thursday.
"We have already been contacted by investors from Asia and the United States who showed interest in the project," a senior transport ministry official said.

Under the plan, which still has to be endorsed by the finance ministry, strategic foreign investors would be offered a 49 percent stake in the airline. The remaining 51 percent would be turned into nominal shares to be sold through the Bucharest stock exchange.
No official deadline has been set by the ministry to implement the project, but the official said privatisation of Tarom would start "as soon as possible".
"The reason why we prefer Romanian investors to have a controlling stake in Tarom is because we think that our flag carrier should remain a company of national interest," he said.
The ministry was also considering the possibility of selling more than 49 percent to foreigners, with the government retaining a golden share to give it veto rights.
Tarom is fighting hard to overcome financial problems including internal and external debts as well as a drop in passenger and cargo traffic.

A restructuring programme including lay-offs, the sale of its outdated Soviet-made planes and purchase of modern aircraft, is under way to upgrade the company and make it more attractive, the official said.
The airline is also considering plans to buy eight new Boeing 737-300 aircraft for medium-haul flights and Franco-Italian ATRs for domestic and regional routes.
Tarom's international routes are served by two A-310 Airbus planes, five Boeing 737s and six BAC 1-11 aircraft.
